newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold ends at day's high in HK on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Gold ends at day's high in HK on short-covering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended at its day's high on Wednesday, climbing from New York's overnight finish on short-covering interest, dealers said.
"The market players were shortcovering, believing that gold had seen its lowest point and was recovering, but not too much," said a dealer at a local investment house.
Bullion ended at US$340.50/341.00 an ounce, up from New York's US$339.70/340.20 close on Tuesday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$339.00/50.

"The immediate gold trend is uncertain as the market lacks a clear direction," another dealer added. "I think the price will stay range-bound, with upside resistance at US$342 and support seen at US$338."
Local gold ended HK$13 higher at HK$3,154 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -3.05 from its previous fix at -1.00.
